subject: Private upgrade: network playcall & staged rollback ladder
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: ops-sre@acmehealth.com, acme-procurement@acmehealth.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com, vendor-ops@cloudvendor.com
Date: Sun, 11 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private upgrade: network playcall & staged rollback ladder

Hi team,

Following our preflight run and the compatibility tests last week, proposed maintenance plan for the Private (VPC) upgrade that will roll kernel+runtime v2.4.1 -> v2.5.0 across the customer clusters. This thread is the single source for the playcall and the rollback ladder; please confirm the windows and owners below.

High-level goals:
- Apply security and performance kernels in v2.5.0 (TLS fixes + packet processing optimizations).
- Preserve pinned model variants; no model version changes during this window.
- Limit user-facing latency increase to <200ms p90 via staged canaries and KV-cache warmup.

Proposed schedule (UTC-7):
- Wed Jul 21 02:00-06:00 — Narrow maintenance window across primary AZs (light traffic, customer agreed).
- Jul 21 02:00-02:30 — Canary tranche (5% of nodes), validation hooks run.
- Jul 21 02:30-04:00 — Progressive ramp (25% -> 60%).
- Jul 21 04:00-06:00 — Full tranche for pinned nodes; guardrail checks and audit.

Key technical notes:
- Version pinning: We will set runtime pin to 2.5.0 on a per-pool basis. Pin changes will be staged via the control plane; pinsets are reversible and will be recorded in the deploy audit log.
- Network gating: A/B traffic steering using load-balancer weights + health probe. If health probes fail for >3 minutes in the canary, automatic rollback to 2.4.1 is triggered for that pool.
- KV/cache: Warmup script will pre-populate popular prefixes for 30m pre-canary; full cache hit-rate and miss patterns logged to the console.
- Circuit-breaker criteria: p95 latency >450ms, increased 5xx rate >1% sustained for 5 minutes, or cache-thrashing indicator.

Attachments: network-diagram-v3.png, rollback-ladder.xlsx, canary-runbook.pdf (see links below).

Action items (please reply with owners):
- Confirm maintenance window and blackout exceptions (Acme SRE).
- Canary validation test owner (Redwood infra lead).
- Network ops escalation contact (CloudVendor).
- Doc sign-off for rollback criteria and runbook.

I'll hold a 30-minute playcall on Tue Jul 20 09:00 PT to walk the sequence. Please ack and list any objections or regulatory constraints.

Thanks,
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Director, Private Deployments | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com

--

Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private upgrade: network playcall & staged rollback ladder

Ack — thanks for the summary, Jonas. A few operational clarifications and a small ask before the playcall: 

1) Rollback ladder detail: please add explicit manual abort steps in the spreadsheet for network flaps vs application regressions. Automatic rollback is fine for probe failures, but operator-led rollback is needed for nuanced degradations (we should call out a single decision owner).

2) Health probes: define both LB-level and app-level probes we’ll rely on. LB-only could hide an app-level KV leak. I propose the canary validation includes: LB-probe pass, /internal/health p95 < 250ms, and KV miss-rate < 15% over 10m.

3) Escalation chain: Add CloudVendor on-call + Redwood infra on-call rotation to the runbook header (I’ve left placeholders in canary-runbook.pdf).

4) Maintenance exceptions: Acme mentioned a downstream billing batch that runs at 03:30 UTC — if that’s true we need to compress the window or move to a different night. @ops-sre@acmehealth.com can you confirm?

I can take the canary validation owner if Jonas + Kar want me on that.

Laura Bennett
Sr Engineering Manager, Platform Ops | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

Thanks Jonas — appreciate the detailed plan. A couple of items from our side: 

- Confirmed: we do have a billing batch at 03:30 UTC in the primary region, but it’s low-latency (single-minute window). We prefer not to interrupt it. Can you shift the main tranche by 30 minutes later (start canary 02:30 -> 03:00 local) or compress the full-tranche cutoff to 05:30? Either option works for us if it reduces risk to billing.

- We need assurance that audit logs and request tracing are retained for 90 days for this upgrade (compliance team request). Can Redwood extend audit log retention for the AcmeCustomer org for the maintenance TTL?

- For emergency rollback, can we get a short DocuSign-ready approval template? Procurement prefers a one-click sign-off by a designated Acme approver to trigger operator rollback. That’ll speed the decision path.

Happy to join the Tue playcall.

—Acme SRE (Priya Malhotra)
ops-sre@acmehealth.com

Thanks — good catches. Quick responses and next steps: 

1) Window change: we will move the canary + ramp + rollout 30 minutes later per your preference: new schedule Wed Jul 21 02:30-06:30 local (UTC-7). I’ll update the runbook and spreadsheet.

2) Audit logs/retention: Redwood infra will enable a 90-day retention snapshot and export for Acme. @neha.kapoor will coordinate the export job and provide the S3 link in the runbook.

3) DocuSign-ready rollback approval: procurement ask acknowledged; I’ll circulate a short pre-populated approval template to acme-procurement@acmehealth.com to accelerate emergency rollback.

4) Ownership and decision path: Laura will be canary validation owner, Kar + Neha are fallback leads, and Jonas will be the final decision arbiter if there’s disagreement. I’ll record these roles in rollback-ladder.xlsx and add the manual abort steps Laura requested.

5) Playcall: Tue Jul 20 09:00 PT confirmed — calendar invite sent. Please have SRE and procurement on the line.
